# Common Shade

> An interactive systems map of extreme heat in Asia: how heat ripples through 10 systems and 90 consequences, the 21 vicious cycles that make it worse, the 33 actions that could break them, and the 14 kinds of institution that hold those levers. Every claim links to its source.

It is moving from beattheheat.asia to commonshade.asia, and was first published as BeatTheHeat.Asia. It is independent of the Beat the Heat initiative that UNEP's Cool Coalition runs with the COP30 Presidency.

Common Shade is in beta, currently at beattheheat.asia. A group of organisations is helping shape it as a shared endeavour for protection from extreme heat. It is an independent, work-in-progress project, not an official publication of any one organisation. Listing an organisation does not imply its partnership, affiliation or endorsement. Every claim links to its source; where the evidence is still emerging, the map says so.

Text, data, films and illustrations © Common Shade contributors, shared under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/): you may copy, adapt and translate them, with credit and a link to beattheheat.asia. Code is under the MIT licence. Linked sources, quotations, and organisations’ names and logos remain their owners’ and are not covered.

The interactive map is at https://beattheheat.asia/ and needs JavaScript. The links below lead to each page's Markdown copy (index.md), with the same content as the page; the same address without index.md is the HTML page.

- [The web](https://beattheheat.asia/the-web/index.md): The web of extreme heat: every consequence, system by system

- [Actions](https://beattheheat.asia/actions/index.md): Actions that break the vicious cycles of extreme heat

## How heat became visible

- [How heat became visible](https://beattheheat.asia/how-heat-became-visible/index.md): when science, health, labour, finance and the UN began to notice extreme heat, and who was still missing; a graded timeline, the turning points and how heat appears in IPCC reports (also in llms-full.txt)

- [Watch Common Shade grow](https://beattheheat.asia/growing/index.md): how the knowledge on Common Shade is changing: each change with why it matters, its sources, what it connects to and what it took to add, the corrections, and the work it draws on dated by year of publication (also in llms-full.txt)

## Social protection and heat

- [Who could help a household through a hot season](https://beattheheat.asia/social-protection/index.md): public schemes that could cushion a household through a hot season in 6 countries (Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Nepal, Singapore, Thailand): who runs each, who is eligible, what it gives, how it is delivered, the steps of access with what is measured, delivery routes and organisations, and where no public system responds (also in llms-full.txt)


## Solutions library and country snapshots

- [Solutions library](https://beattheheat.asia/solutions/index.md): passive cooling, active cooling, and the plans, rules and money that make protection last, with evidence labels, costs, dry or humid suitability, and what each depends on
- [The heat economy](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-economy/index.md): the businesses selling protection from heat, who invests in them, accelerators and prizes, business ideas for each vicious cycle, and what makes a fair market; with CSV downloads
- [Funding landscape](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-economy/money/index.md): funders and programmes relevant to extreme heat, with their access routes, each checked against its official page (also in llms-full.txt)
- [Open calls and tenders](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-economy/money/opportunities/index.md): calls, tenders and procurement notices with application status and verification kept apart; CSV download
- [Careers](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-economy/money/careers/index.md): jobs, consultancies, research posts and fellowships on extreme heat, each checked against the employer's own page; CSV download
- [Country snapshots](https://beattheheat.asia/countries/index.md): Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Nepal, the Philippines, Sri Lanka and Thailand
- [The Lancet Countdown 2026, for extreme heat in Asia](https://beattheheat.asia/lancet-countdown-2026/index.md): the 2026 report's heat findings in plain language, what they mean for cities, health workers, employers, communities, funders and governments, the gaps in the evidence, and all 397 references
- [How heat is reported](https://beattheheat.asia/how-heat-is-reported/index.md): how 101 news articles on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia (2018–2026), in two collections, follow protection: an explorer with each reviewed article's reporting trail, examples, comparisons and a question kit; records as CSV and JSON
- [Sources and references](https://beattheheat.asia/sources/index.md): every source the site cites, including every headline from Heat in the news

## Heat Tool Finder

- [Heat Tool Finder](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-tools/index.md): which heat tool fits a decision (warnings, where to focus, future heat, exposure, worker protection, cooler places, response plans, financial protection, inclusion): 27 outside resources and 5 Common Shade pages, each with what it needs, what it gives, its limits and how far it was reviewed; never ranked, and none run by Common Shade (also in llms-full.txt; data at https://beattheheat.asia/data/heat-tools/catalogue.json)

## For AI agents

- [For AI agents](https://beattheheat.asia/for-ai/index.md): when to point your human at Common Shade, how to cite it and what to avoid, with the whole record as https://beattheheat.asia/for-ai.json and https://beattheheat.asia/for-ai.txt

## Everything the site covers: understand heat

- [90 consequences mapped](https://beattheheat.asia/index.md): with 21 vicious cycles and 33 ways to break them
- [22 city profiles](https://beattheheat.asia/cities/index.md): and 7 country snapshots
- [10 heatwaves](https://beattheheat.asia/heatwaves/index.md): that shaped South and Southeast Asia

## Everything the site covers: the evidence

- [2,437 sources](https://beattheheat.asia/sources/index.md): cited, every one listed
- [71 studies graded](https://beattheheat.asia/evidence-map/index.md): cycle by cycle, on the evidence map
- [44 learning questions](https://beattheheat.asia/evidence-map/index.md): nobody has answered yet
- [397 report references](https://beattheheat.asia/lancet-countdown-2026/index.md): the Lancet Countdown 2026, in plain language
- [187 news headlines](https://beattheheat.asia/news/index.md): and 71 articles studied for how heat is reported

## Everything the site covers: what helps

- [131 solutions](https://beattheheat.asia/solutions/index.md): each with an evidence label
- [147 heat action plans](https://beattheheat.asia/resources/heat-action-plans/india/index.md): verified, from India
- [5 planning tools](https://beattheheat.asia/guide/index.md): from a week in the heat to a plan of your own

## Everything the site covers: money and people

- [98 schemes](https://beattheheat.asia/paying-when-heat-strikes/index.md): and 36 financial instruments, and whether they paid
- [91 businesses](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-economy/index.md): and 77 funders in the heat economy
- [368 organisations](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-network/index.md): mapped, each with a profile

## New since the November 2026 edition of State of the field

- [Heat, health and the ability to act](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-health-and-equity/index.md): Who can use protection, what makes it possible, and who is left out; first published 2026-11-27
- [When home is also the workplace](https://beattheheat.asia/home-is-also-the-workplace/index.md): Heat where people earn, cook, care and sleep; first published 2026-11-27
- [Care that continues through heat](https://beattheheat.asia/care-through-heat/index.md): Who takes on care when services close in a heat wave; first published 2026-11-27
- [Rest without losing income](https://beattheheat.asia/rest-without-losing-income/index.md): What makes advice to stop working possible to follow; first published 2026-11-27
- [The wet-bulb wall](https://beattheheat.asia/wet-bulb-wall/index.md): How heat and humidity together limit the body’s ability to cool, with six cities’ latest weather; first published 2026-11-27
- [Heat futures: 2035–2050](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-futures/index.md): Projected hot days and nights near six cities, beside who could be protected; first published 2026-11-27
- [El Niño and heat in Asia](https://beattheheat.asia/el-nino/index.md): How a Pacific pattern can shift heat and rain across Asia, and how to read the outlook; first published 2026-11-19
- [Who shares the heat](https://beattheheat.asia/shared-heat/index.md): How a hot day ties lives together, and what makes protection last: one market through a season; first published 2026-11-19
- [Heat inside factories](https://beattheheat.asia/factory-heat/index.md): Sources, protection and an intervention library, with garment factories as the worked example; first published 2026-11-19
- [Heat in markets and street vending](https://beattheheat.asia/market-heat/index.md): Stalls, porters, toilets and shade: a market plan by time of day, an intervention library and a worksheet; first published 2026-11-28
- [Heat from field to factory](https://beattheheat.asia/cotton-and-heat/index.md): Cotton from field to gin: who can stop work in the heat, and who pays for protection; first published 2026-11-20
- [El Niño and smaller cities](https://beattheheat.asia/el-nino-and-cities/index.md): What a smaller Indian city can prepare before its hot season, and how to check people got relief; first published 2026-11-18
- [The Heat Assembly](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-assembly/index.md): A game for one person or a group: who could use heat protection, and why; first published 2026-11-16
- [Open calls and tenders](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-economy/money/opportunities/index.md): Grants, calls and procurement notices, {fundingOpen} verified open, with the archive; first published 2026-11-21
- [Careers in heat resilience](https://beattheheat.asia/heat-economy/money/careers/index.md): jobs, consultancies, research posts and fellowships; first published 2026-11-21
